📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment. Whether someone prefers a classic Jane Austen novel or a Heartstopper graphic novel, research suggests that reading for pleasure is associated with better mental health, stronger empathy, and a lower risk of dementia.

Researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups. Their collaboration is part of the National Year of Reading, an initiative encouraging more people to make reading part of their lives.

In a recent development, cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr. Christelle Langley began exploring the subject while writing their 2025 book, Brain Boost: Healthy Habits for a Happier Life. They discovered that reading for enjoyment was connected to a remarkably wide range of positive outcomes, yet the amount of research specifically examining these benefits was surprisingly limited.

According to recent reports, in a review published in Psychological Medicine, Sahakian and Langley joined Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, to examine the available evidence. Their findings suggest that the format and type of reading matter less than the enjoyment people get from it. They also highlight how reading together, whether through book clubs or parents sharing stories with children, can provide additional benefits.

Industry observers note that professor Sahakian remarked: "Reading is a great way to support our brain health, develop vital cognitive skills and boost our well-being. It's something we ought to be encouraging from an early age, given the increasing evidence of its benefits, particularly to children, but really, it's never too late to start, and it can bring benefits throughout our lives and into old age.".

Reading Early in Life Is Linked to Better Brain Development.

Despite the growing evidence of its advantages, reading for enjoyment has become less common among young people. Surveys indicate that reading rates among children and teenagers have fallen to their lowest recorded levels, with particularly steep challenges among teenage boys and children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

Industry observers note that even children who are least enthusiastic about reading recognize that it can help them academically. Nearly half acknowledge that books and other reading materials can introduce them to unfamiliar words or teach them something upcoming.

One of the most compelling studies examined more than 10,000 young people. Conducted by Sahakian, Langley, and their colleagues, the research found that children who started reading for pleasure at an early age tended to perform better in several important areas. These included attention, memory, and executive functioning, the mental abilities involved in planning, decision-making, and managing behavior.

According to recent reports, early readers also showed stronger academic performance, experienced fewer mental health problems, and were more likely to develop healthier daily routines. In particular, they tended to get more sleep and spend less time using screens.

Industry observers note that dr. Langley remarked: "Given how beneficial reading for pleasure is at a young age, we should be doing everything we can to introduce children and young people to reading. The important thing is to find something they'd really enjoy reading about - it might be a TV program or a game - and use this as a way in. Reading comics and graphic novels could also be a helpful introduction as they might be seen as less intimidating, maybe less boring, than novels.".

The academic advantages may extend beyond language and literacy. Studies have also connected reading with stronger mathematical performance. Researchers suggest this relationship may arise because both activities rely on some of the same mental abilities, including language processing, memory, and executive function.

Just Five Minutes of Reading May Reduce Stress.

Industry observers note that the benefits of reading do not disappear after childhood. Among adults, surveys have associated reading for enjoyment with improved emotional well-being, greater relaxation, and reduced stress. Readers also tend to report more empathy, a deeper understanding of other people, and greater openness to viewpoints different from their own.

Industry observers note that for many people, books are an especially appealing way to unwind. Reading ranks as the most popular approach to stress relief, with nearly two in five adults (38%) identifying it as their preferred way to relax.

A neuroscience study commissioned by The Queen's Reading Room in 2024 found that spending just five minutes reading fiction could lower stress by as much as 20%. The study also reported improvements in concentration and problem-solving abilities, along with a reduced sense of loneliness.

Books may even provide more comfort than some traditional relaxation habits. In one survey, more respondents remarked they turned to reading (35%) for comfort than to drinking wine (31%) or taking a hot bath (10%).

Reading Linked to Lower Dementia and Alzheimer's Risk.

In a recent development, as people get older, the potential advantages of reading may become especially meaningful. Research has associated mentally stimulating leisure activities, including reading, with slower cognitive decline and a reduced likelihood of developing dementia.

One study followed nearly 5,500 adults aged 55 and older for five years. Participants who regularly took part in activities such as reading were significantly less likely to develop cognitive impairment during the study period.

Industry observers note that another investigation reported an even more striking association. People who read newspapers, magazines, and books had a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

It has been revealed that these findings suggest that keeping the mind engaged through reading may support cognitive health in later life. However, the researchers emphasize that most of the available studies identify associations rather than proving that reading itself prevents dementia.

How Reading May Change the Structure of the Brain.

What could explain the many benefits associated with reading? Brain imaging research offers some intriguing clues.

Industry observers note that studies have identified differences in brain structure associated with reading, particularly in regions responsible for language, learning, emotional regulation, and executive control. These differences include greater brain volume and larger cortical areas in certain regions, as well as thicker cortex in areas notable for language processing.

Researchers have also observed stronger connections within the brain's white matter, which helps different regions communicate and supports the processing of language.

Although much of this evidence is correlational, some research suggests that reading-related training can directly influence the brain's physical structure.

In one small study involving 11 children with dyslexia between the ages of 7 and 11, researchers tested an eight-week training program designed to strengthen reading abilities. The exercises involved mental imagery, articulation, and tracing letters, combinations of letters, and words.

Sources indicate that following the program, the children demonstrated significant improvements in reading skills. Brain scans also revealed increases in gray matter volume in vital regions, providing evidence that reading interventions can be accompanied by measurable structural changes in the brain.

Why Reading Together May Offer Even Greater Benefits.

Industry observers note that reading does not have to be a solitary activity. Researchers suggest that sharing books with other people can add a valuable social dimension, creating opportunities for connection and potentially improving both mental and physical well-being.

Industry observers note that the Queen's Reading Room has made this idea a central part of its mission. Rolled out on social media in January 2021, the initiative originally provided a way for people to exchange book recommendations and stay connected during pandemic lockdowns.

It has since expanded into an international community reaching more than 12 million people across 184 countries. Through its flagship festival, neuroscience research, and other programs, the charity works to make reading a more prominent part of everyday life.

Its activities also extend to homeless shelters and domestic violence refuges, where shared reading is used as a therapeutic resource to help people during recovery.

The social connections created through reading groups may be particularly valuable for older adults, who can face increased isolation and reduced opportunities to participate in physically demanding activities.

Professor Sahakian said: "Shared reading groups and book clubs appear to provide additional benefits through social interaction. They can help people feel less isolated and more connected to others, which has been shown to reduce the risk of dementia.

"While these clubs can be fun and beneficial at any age, they're perfect for older people who may not be so mobile - they might not be able to go out as an exercise group or a cycling group, but a reading group is something most people can enjoy.".

The researchers' overall message is that people can benefit from reading at any stage of life. Whether someone enjoys novels, newspapers, comics, or stories shared with friends, making time for reading may help support cognitive health, emotional well-being, and social connection.

Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, added: "At The Queen's Reading Room, we have seen first-hand the transformative power of individual and shared reading to change lives. Books truly do make life better, and we're excited to do our bit to help everyone, everywhere, make more room for reading.".

Materials provided by University of Cambridge. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Weekly Rundown: Waystar integrates into Google Cloud’s Gemini for healthcare; Oracle debuts AI agents for clinical trials" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Stay up to date on the latest in health tech, digital health and health AI news with this weekly brief. Read below for news from the week of Nov. 16 to 27.

Waystar said Tuesday it will integrate its AI-driven revenue cycle solutions into Google Cloud’s recently declared Gemini for healthcare solution.

Recent findings suggest that the integration reflects an expanded partnership between Waystar and Google Cloud. Through it, consumers will have increased access to Waystar AltitudeAI innovations, advanced analytics and revenue cycle insights.

“By bringing Waystar's AI-powered revenue cycle capabilities into Gemini for healthcare, we're helping providers simplify some of the most complex operational and financial tasks in care delivery,” stated Aashima Gupta, Google Cloud managing director of healthcare, in a statement. “Together, we are unifying data and workflows in a secure, governed workspace that drives better outcomes across the healthcare ecosystem.”.

OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT’s health capabilities across various channels, it said Thursday.

The tech giant’s Health feature is expanding to desktop app, Androids and its personal AI agents—dubbed dots.

Among the fresh capabilities include:.

ChatGPT Health is currently available to Free, Go, Plus, and Pro consumers in the U.S., while dots are available to Pro users.

Oracle released a upcoming agentic experience for life science organizations to improve clinical trial operations.

According to recent reports, oracle Life Science AI Agents is presently available for early adopters with a focus on portfolio monitoring, trial planning and conduct. The company looks to expand into clinical development domains, including data management, post-trial analytics and trial design.

Agents are designed to work with human oversight, executives say.

Oracle Health and Life Sciences EVP and General Manager Seema Verma noted in a statement clinical development requires companies to “coordinate complex operational activity.”.

It has been revealed that “We are bringing AI-assisted intelligence into clinical trial operations to help organizations to monitor performance, identify emerging risks, and coordinate responses across the trial lifecycle,” Verma remarked. “By combining Oracle’s Life Sciences applications, AI-assisted capabilities, connected data services, on a secure, scalable cloud infrastructure, we are helping organizations coordinate clinical research workflows and operational decisions across their clinical trial environments.”.

Agentic organization Artera confirmed the roll out of an intake solution using AI Agents to collect, check and complete information throughout the patient visit.

Artera Intake has three core workflows, executives say: pre-visit intake, in-office and walk-in intake and complex form and consent digitization. The workflows are housed in a newly introduced Intake Hub, according to the Nov. 19 announcement.

Chief Product and Strategy Officer Zach Wood said in a statement what differentiates the solution from others is “where it starts.”.

“Most intake solutions are built first, and providers have to change their workflows to fit them,” Wood said. “We start with the provider. We learn how their teams and patients actually move through intake, then build the agentic solution around that, together.”.

Wood continued, “That starting point shapes everything that follows, and is designed to drive faster adoption, more completed intake and real value for practices.”.

Amazon Connect Health declared Nov. 17 the launch of expanded patient access capabilities through the agentic solution.

As of the date of the announcement, four newly introduced capabilities are generally available to people: appointment management, prescription management, information assistance and password reset.

The organization indicates the expansion builds on the foundation of Amazon Connect Health, which included patient verification, patient insights, ambient documentation and more.

One health system using the tool is Philadelphia-based Temple Health. AVP of Patient Access Joseph Alfonsi said in a statement the tool has handled patient verification on thousands of calls weekly since the system went live in June.

“Building on that success, we’re excited to expand agentic patient access capabilities for prescription management, portal password resets, and information assistance,” Alfonsi said. “Our patients shouldn’t have to wait until business hours—or wait on hold—to manage routine tasks. Now they can verify once and take care of everyday needs in a single call, any time of day, and our team can focus on the conversations where a human touch matters most.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage applications increased last week, despite high interest rates, inflation concerns, and a wobbly stock market.

For the week ending Nov. 20, the Mortgage Bankers Association's Market Composite Index—a measure of total mortgage loan application volume—increased 6.1% on a seasonally adjusted basis from one week earlier.

The Purchase Index, which measures the volume of mortgage applications to purchase a single-family home, increased 5% from one week earlier after seasonal adjustment, though purchase applications are down 16% from a year ago.

The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed mortgages with conforming loan balances jumped to 7.38% this week, an increase from last week's rate of 7.31%, according to MBA calculations, and it's the highest level in five weeks.

According to recent reports, A separate survey from Freddie Mac showed mortgage rates rose to 7.28%, up from  7.11% last week. A year ago at this time, the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.26%.

"While mortgage rates increased slightly on a weekly average basis, rates declined over the course of the week, which likely spurred purchase application activity,” said Joel Kan, MBA’s vice president and deputy chief economist.

“Purchase applications reached their strongest weekly pace since September but remained well behind last year’s pace," he added.

Kan also noted that the share of borrowers relying on riskier adjustable-rate mortgage loans jumped to 11.5%—its highest level in more than a year.

"At 6.39%, the ARM mortgage rate was nearly a full percentage lower than the 30-year fixed rate last week," he stated.

The share of FHA loan applications decreased to 15.9% from 16.1% the prior week. The VA share of total applications decreased to 12.4% from 12.8% the prior week. And the USDA share of total applications remained unchanged at 0.5%.

The refinance share of mortgage activity decreased to 40.1% from 41.1% the previous week, but was 51% lower than the same week one year ago, as homeowners remain locked in to their lower interest rates.

Recent findings suggest that "Refinance activity was flat over the week with conventional applications showing a small increase while VA refinances dropped more than 11%," Kan said. The latest mortgage application data comes following a week of stock market volatility. On Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 briefly plunged into correction territory, defined as a 10% decline from their last peak.

Sources indicate that the sell-off, driven by a wipeout in tech and AI stocks, came a day after Anthropic raised a staggering $81.34 billion during its IPO on Thursday, lifting the organization's valuation to $1.414 trillion.Adding to the economic stress was an announcement on Wednesday from President Donald Trump that he's proposed latest tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU, and a dozen other major U.S. trading partners to take effect next year.

According to recent reports, mortgage rates are calculated based on several economic factors, while your loan term and credit score also influence the mortgage rate you qualify for. On the economic side, rates tend to track the 10-year Treasury note, since most 30-year mortgages are paid off or refinanced in roughly eight to 11 years.

That makes the duration on the loans roughly comparable, and mortgage lenders use the 10-year Treasury as a benchmark for setting rates, adding on a risk premium.

Long-term yields for Treasury notes are determined by a number of factors, including the supply of and demand for U.S. government debt, and investor expectations for inflation over the life of the bonds.

Scientists discover a hidden eye disease that slowly steals night vision

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A newly identified genetic eye disease can gradually interfere with night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of the visual field.
  • An international research team, including scientists at the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, traced the condition to a gene already associated with another form of vision loss.
  • In a recent development, although the condition has not yet received an official name, researchers are calling it EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly identified genetic eye disease can gradually interfere with night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of the visual field. The condition may be especially difficult to recognize because people can maintain good eyesight for much of their lives before noticeable problems develop.

An international research team, including scientists at the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, traced the condition to a gene already associated with another form of vision loss. However, the two diseases affect eyesight in strikingly different ways. The previously known disorder primarily damages central vision, while the newly discovered condition affects peripheral vision and the ability to see in darkness.

In a recent development, although the condition has not yet received an official name, researchers are calling it EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD). It is linked to a specific genetic variant known as p.Arg140Trp in the EFEMP1 gene. This change causes an unusually thick accumulation of material between cells in the eye.

A Genetic Discovery That Began Decades Ago.

The investigation traces back to 1998, when doctors documented an unusual pattern of vision loss in a family in the United States. As researchers uncovered new genetic evidence, they were able to connect those findings to families in Europe who demonstrated similar symptoms.

Sources indicate that the study, published in JAMA Ophthalmology, examined three unrelated families from different countries who carried the p.Arg140Trp variant. Their symptoms were compared with those of another family carrying a different change in the same gene, called p.Arg345Trp, which is associated with the previously recognized disease affecting central vision.

The international collaboration included researchers from Penn Medicine, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Basel, Charles University, and the University of Bonn.

In a recent development, at first, scientists suspected that the unusual symptoms in the original family might be caused by a different genetic disorder. Testing, however, failed to identify the variants responsible for that condition.

"The different disease expression in this family was thought to be similar to a condition caused by C1QTNF5 gene variants. However, none of the variants associated with that disease were found," said Artur V. Cideciyan, PhD, an ophthalmology researcher and co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Our collaborators then discovered a new variant in the EFEMP1 gene that normally causes a different disease where the macula, which is tied to central vision, is affected first.".

How the Fresh Eye Disease Affects Night Vision.

The researchers found that the newly identified condition develops gradually in the outer regions of the retina. Located at the back of the eye, the retina detects incoming light and transforms it into signals that the brain uses to create visual images.

Unlike the previously known EFEMP1 disorder, which initially affects the macula and central vision, this newly identified disease begins in the peripheral retina. People may see normally for much of their lives before gradually noticing that their side vision is narrowing or that seeing in dim surroundings has become more difficult.

Problems may be particularly noticeable around dusk or at night, when the eyes must rely more heavily on specialized light-sensitive cells called rods.

In a recent development, one reason the disease is challenging to diagnose is that these cells may initially show no visible structural damage. The gradual progression of symptoms can make the condition even harder to recognize.

In a recent development, however, the researchers identified a potentially valuable early clue. In affected individuals, rod cells take unusually long to recover when the eyes move from bright surroundings into darkness. This abnormal response can be detected even when the retina still appears structurally normal.

"We can detect a major abnormality in the way rod photoreceptors recover in darkness with retinas that still look structurally intact," Cideciyan mentioned. "This gives us a functional marker of disease at a stage when photoreceptor cells have not yet been lost.".

The finding suggests that changes in how the retina functions may reveal the disease before the light-sensitive cells responsible for vision begin to disappear.

What the Discovery Could Mean for Age-Related Vision Loss.

An crucial question remains unanswered: How many people carry this newly identified genetic variant?

Researchers suspect the condition is relatively uncommon, but they do not yet have enough information to determine its prevalence. Larger investigations will be necessary to establish how frequently the variant occurs and how many people may be affected.

Industry observers note that beyond identifying another inherited eye disorder, the findings could help scientists better understand why vision deteriorates with age. Studying rare genetic diseases can reveal biological processes that may also contribute to much more widespread retinal conditions.

"Aging is a risk factor for many medical conditions, including retinal diseases such as age-related macular degeneration, the most common retinal condition of aging," mentioned Tomas S. Aleman, MD, a professor of ophthalmology and the other co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Lessons learned from these infrequent, late-onset genetic eye diseases offer glimpses at possible mechanisms of disease for much more frequent retinal problems.".

It has been revealed that by revealing how different changes in a single gene can produce distinct patterns of vision loss, the research adds to scientists' understanding of inherited retinal disease. It also highlights the potential importance of detecting changes in visual function before damage becomes apparent in the retina's structure.

The study received support from the University of Edinburgh Chancellor's Fellowship award, RS Macdonald Charitable Trust Seedcorn Award, the BrightFocus Foundation (M2024009N), the German Research Foundation (532367710), the Medical Research Council (MC_UU_00035/9, MC_UU_00007/10), the Swiss National Science Foundation (204285), the Ministry of Health of the Czech Republic (NW24-06-00083), Charles University in Prague (UNCE/24/MED/022 and SVV 2600631), and the Samuel G. Jacobson, MD, PhD, Memorial Fund.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Moving can be a time-consuming process, but it doesn't need to be stressful. We have some tips to help you enjoy a smooth move from your old home to the upcoming. With the right system in place, there is no need to be overwhelmed by the move.

Before you make the move, check out these 5 packing tips.

It has been revealed that A common mistake people make when moving is to pack all of their belongings and move them, only to realize upon unpacking that many of the items should have been donated, sold, or thrown out. Before you pack, ruthlessly declutter your home. Packing things only to get rid of them at the new house is a waste of your time and money.

Some questions to ask yourself as you declutter before packing are:.

Industry observers note that as you pack and move, things are bound to get misplaced. To avoid the stress of a missing document or essential information, keep a folder (either physical, digital, or both) where you won't misplace it that is filled with essential paperwork. This might include:.

Industry observers note that greg Dallaire - Green Bay Real Estate Expert notes, "Be sure to set up any utilities in the new place to be turned on and ready when you arrive. Even if it means paying for utilities at two places for a brief overlap, it is often worth the convenience. In addition to basics like water and power, call ahead to make sure you will have internet, TV, and any other services you need.".

This is also a great time to move additional services to the new address, like security, pest control, or house cleaning.

It has been revealed that even if you are moving all in one day from one Calgary home to another, don't count on being able to unpack everything you need on night one. Instead, pack a suitcase with a few days' worth of clothes and necessities for everyone in the house. This way, you can settle into your new home without scrambling to find a towel or toothbrush before spending your first night there.

Industry observers note that the suitcase should include more than just your change of clothes and toiletries. Anything you might need for 2-3 days should be packed in it, including:.

As you pack, or have your movers pack, label each box with not just the contents inside but the room it should be placed in at the upcoming home. This way, whether you have professional movers, a team of friends and family, or just your own household, it will be easy to make sure each box lands in the proper place.

One of the easiest ways to do this is by color coding. Assign a color to each room and label accordingly. For example, let's say the kitchen is blue. All boxes that should be brought to the kitchen will be labeled with blue tape, and on move-in day you can hang a large blue paper in the kitchen. This simple system will make unpacking much smoother.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:54 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Rajiv Ramaswami is stepping down from his role as chief executive of Nutanix Inc., six years after he joined the hyperconverged cloud infrastructure organization from its rival VMware Inc.

Recent findings suggest that in a letter to organization employees, Ramaswami (pictured) mentioned he’s going to continue in the role for the time being while he works with Nutanix’s board of directors to identify a successor and assist with the transition. “After that, I will continue to serve as a senior advisor to the company for a period of time,” he said in the letter.

Ramaswami, who is 60 years old, did not give any reason for his coming departure, but the letter seems to indicate that he’s not ready to retire just yet.

Industry observers note that “Our next CEO will inherit a strong platform, a loyal customer base and, most importantly, an exceptional team,” Ramaswami wrote. “Until then, my focus remains on leading this organization and nothing about our day-to-day priorities changes. I am committed to helping our next leader succeed, and my ask of you, as always, is to continue to focus on executing as we go through this leadership transition.”.

Ramaswami added that Nutanix has hired an executive search firm to lead the hunt for his successor. The news came as the tech giant delivered its first-quarter earnings report, posting modest year-over-year gains in profit and revenue.

The tech giant reported adjusted earnings of 73 cents per share, beating Wall Street’s target of 61 cents per share by a strong margin. Revenue for the period came to $772.4 million, up 15% from a year earlier and above the Street’s forecast of $762.7 million.

Nutanix’s outlook for the current quarter is strong, with the company guiding for sales of between $820 million and $830 million, compared with the Street’s consensus estimate of $820.4 million. However, the full-year picture is a little less rosy, with Nutanix guiding for annual sales of $3.18 billion to $3.23 billion. The midpoint of that range trails the Street’s forecast of $3.22 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue.

Investors did not take the news very well. The cautious full-year guidance compared with the uncertainty over leadership prompted many to sell, and Nutanix’s stock was down 8% after-hours, having already fallen more than 5% during the regular trading session, on a down day for many tech stocks.

Recent findings suggest that virginia Gambale, of the board at Nutanix, hailed the “tremendous impact” Ramaswami had on the firm during his six-year tenure. “Rajiv led the company’s transformation to subscription software, built a loyal and expanding global enterprise base and established a technology portfolio that we believe positions us well for the AI era,” she noted. “We’re focused on selecting an exceptional leader who can build on that foundation.”.

Sources indicate that in a conference call with analysts, Ramaswami remarked he believes the company is embarking on the third major chapter in its history. The first chapter, before his arrival, saw the company establish itself as the leader of the hyperconverged infrastructure industry. Chapter two began when he took over, and saw Nutanix expand from those roots to become a platform company, he said.

“[We have] transformed the company to be profitable while growing and expanding the product portfolio quite significantly, from HCI to a platform that works across clouds, supports external storage and has cloud-native capabilities and now moving into the future with AI capabilities,” Ramaswami said. “Chapter two is well-established at this point and there’s a lot of opportunity in terms of driving growth. I feel like we are in a very good place.”.

According to Ramaswami, Nutanix now stands at an inflection point as it looks to cash in on the latest era of artificial intelligence. “I’ve been talking to the board for a bit about this, as well as in terms of our strategic direction and the timing for succession, and so we came to the conclusion together that this is perhaps the right time,” he told analysts. “[We wanted] to announce it ahead of time as we look for the appropriate next leader.”.

Ramaswami’s departure from the company should at least be a lot smoother than his arrival. Nutanix unveiled it had appointed Ramaswami as its CEO in late 2020, just two days after he quit his role as chief operating officer of its biggest rival, VMware.

Recent findings suggest that VMware was indignant about the manner of his departure, and responded with a lawsuit that accused Ramaswami of breaching his legal and contractual duties to the company by “secretly meeting” with Nutanix’s board to discuss taking over, while continuing to play a leading role in shaping its product and business strategy. The lawsuit was ultimately settled out of court about a year later.

Millennials living in rural areas have 42% more documented chronic conditions on average compared to those in other environments, a new report from athenaInstitute found.

It has been revealed that and, millennials in rural communities are 47% more likely to have at least two chronic conditions. This heavier chronic disease burden extends to other generations as well, analysts note.

Half of Baby Boomers (50.4%) in rural areas have three or more documented conditions, which the report says is “on par” with non-rural individuals in the Silent and Greatest generations.

The 2026 Rural Ambulatory Care Report (PDF) analyzed athenahealth network data across 12.3 million rural patients between 2021 and 2025, as well as more than 30,000 clinicians and 1,861 rural practices across the entire U.S. Factors such as appointment activity, workforce composition, payments and more were examined.

Athenahealth CMO and athenaInstitute co-chair Nele Jessel, M.D., said in a statement the findings show while rural practices are not “standing still in the face of enormous challenges,” there are “limits to how much more they can absorb as patient needs continue to grow.”.

It has been revealed that “They are adapting how they deliver care and finding ways to keep patients connected to the care they need,” Jessel noted. “With renewed focus on rural healthcare, there is a real opportunity to build on what is working by investing in the workforce, technology and models of care that can help these practices continue serving the communities that depend on them.”.

Primary care physicians in rural areas have to wear multiple hats, as specialty care needs at practices are higher in rural communities.

In a recent development, the report found that primary care handles 68.7% of visits involving anxiety or depression diagnoses versus 55.1% in non-rural areas. Moreover, 25% of rural patients with documented anxiety or depression had a substance use disorder—up from 19.8% in non-rural communities.

Data shows rural and non-rural healthcare practices collected roughly the same share of what they were owed by insurers in 2025, but analysts note a difference in patient balances.

Rural practices collected about $70 of every $100 owed, while non-rural practices collected about $78—which analysts say is about a 10% gap.

#202391. A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1191 w)

A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1191 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension.
  • Losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile.
  • In a recent development, the findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension. Scientists have found that losartan can activate brown fat, a specialized type of body fat that burns energy, and improve metabolic activity in mice. The discovery suggests that an existing medication could potentially be repurposed to stimulate brown fat and support metabolic health.

Losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile. In a new study published in Nature, researchers found that the drug increased brown fat activity through a biological mechanism separate from its blood pressure effects. This raises the possibility of developing treatments that activate brown fat without lowering blood pressure.

In a recent development, the findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health. After examining data from more than 100,000 patients, researchers discovered that people with detectable brown fat had lower rates of several medical conditions, including anxiety and depression. This is the first time the research team has reported associations between brown fat and psychiatric health, adding to earlier evidence linking the tissue to better cardiovascular and metabolic health.

In a recent development, the research was led by Paul Cohen at Rockefeller University's Laboratory of Molecular Metabolism, working with Heiko Schöder and Daniel Lafontaine from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC). It expands on research published in 2021, when Cohen's team analyzed approximately 50,000 patients and found that those with more brown fat had substantially lower odds of developing cardiometabolic conditions such as coronary artery disease and type II diabetes.

According to recent reports, "We only looked for a few diagnostic codes in that study, mainly focusing on cardiovascular disease since that's what this tissue has historically been associated with," notes Cohen. "The scope of this new analysis is far more expansive. We doubled our number of patients and considered more than 500 codes, which allowed us to unearth many new insights.".

AI Analysis Reveals New Benefits of Brown Fat.

According to recent reports, to investigate brown fat's relationship with human health, the researchers examined PET/CT scans from more than 100,000 patients who had undergone imaging as part of their cancer monitoring. They focused on scans showing brown adipose tissue, which can be found in six regions of the body, including the neck, armpits, and areas around organs such as the heart and kidneys.

The team used an approach known as reverse translation, which begins with observations in patients and then investigates the biological processes responsible for them. Cohen's laboratory has previously used this strategy to uncover vital details about brown fat and its effects on health.

It has been revealed that nicolás Gómez-Banoy, the study's first author and an endocrinologist and instructor in clinical investigation in Cohen's laboratory, used a machine learning system developed by researchers at MSKCC to measure brown fat activity. The technology allowed him to assess both the total activity in each patient and the activity within each of the six anatomical regions.

It has been revealed that the analysis highlighted that brown fat's location could be just as important as its presence. Activity in particular regions appeared to have stronger associations with certain health conditions, suggesting that brown fat may influence the body differently depending on where it is found.

"For example, the axillary, or armpit, area was linked to a decreased risk of high blood pressure compared to other regions," he says. "But overall, patients with brown fat have better glycemic parameters, lipid profiles, and echocardiographic indices, as well as lower inflammatory markers.".

These findings indicate that people with brown fat tend to have healthier blood sugar levels, blood fat profiles, measures of heart function, and indicators of inflammation.

Common Blood Pressure Drug Activates Brown Fat.

As the researchers investigated medications associated with brown fat activity, they noticed an intriguing pattern. Patients taking angiotensin receptor blockers were more likely to have detectable brown fat on their scans, suggesting that these widely prescribed medications might influence the tissue.

To explore that possibility, the team conducted laboratory experiments using cultured brown fat cells. They found that losartan directly increased the cells' metabolic activity, providing evidence that the drug could stimulate brown fat rather than simply being associated with its presence.

Even more interestingly, the researchers discovered that losartan activated brown fat through molecular pathways different from those responsible for lowering blood pressure. That distinction could be especially valuable for developing future medications that target metabolism without interfering with normal blood pressure regulation.

In a recent development, "The fact that its different effects are mediated by different molecular pathways is advantageous, since it means we could potentially isolate them in future therapies," claims Gómez-Banoy. "That way you would be able to stimulate brown fat in people with normal blood pressure.".

Sources indicate that additional experiments in healthy mice strengthened the findings. Animals given losartan indicated increased energy expenditure, consumed more oxygen, and produced more carbon dioxide, all signs of heightened metabolic activity. Despite these changes, their body weight remained stable.

Brown Fat's Surprising Connection to Mental Health.

Beyond its metabolic effects, brown fat may have a previously unrecognized relationship with psychological well-being. The patient analysis revealed that individuals with detectable brown fat had lower rates of anxiety and depression, extending the tissue's potential health associations beyond the cardiovascular system.

"We know that metabolically healthy people tend to have lower incidence of psychiatric diseases, so it could be that having brown fat makes you more metabolically healthy, and this correlates with fewer psychiatric complications," claims Gómez-Banoy.

The researchers also found an intriguing relationship involving selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or SSRIs, medications commonly prescribed to treat depression. These drugs appeared to suppress brown fat activity, suggesting another possible connection between psychiatric treatments and metabolic regulation.

Recent findings suggest that however, the findings do not suggest that brown fat is beneficial in every respect. The analysis also identified higher rates of osteoporosis and certain skin diseases among people with brown fat, raising questions about possible trade-offs that require further investigation.

The discoveries have opened several avenues for future research. Scientists hope to examine the genetics of people with particularly high brown fat activity, investigate why the tissue is associated with lower rates of anxiety and depression, and determine whether its apparent benefits can be harnessed safely.

According to recent reports, losartan may also be only one of several existing medications worth investigating. The extensive patient analysis identified additional drugs associated with brown fat activity, offering researchers a range of potential candidates for future studies.

Sources indicate that "There were plenty of other medications associated with brown fat activity in our large cohort," Cohen notes. "This is just a start.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that new -home sales surged in October as prices dropped, according to the latest data from the U.S. Census Bureau.

Sales of newly introduced single-family homes hit 701,000 in October, 14.2% above what they were in September and 7.5% above October 2025. Meanwhile, the median sales price hit $391,300, 0.3% below September 2026 and 3.2% below October 2025.

That was driven entirely by a surge in the South, which saw a 36.2% increase from last month and a 24.7% increase from October 2025. Northeast sales plummeted 40.0% month over month and 63.4% year over year, and the Midwest and West also saw declines.

Sources indicate that this comes after new-home sales fell 0.6% month over month, 5.3% year over year in September, to 676,000. New-home sales were running 2.9% below 2025 numbers, Realtor.com® economists found. The median sales price in September for new homes fell 3.9% year over year to $400,400.

Recent findings suggest that realtor.com Senior Economist Joel Berner noted that fresh home sales are still 3% below where they were in the first 10 months of 2025. And housing inventory remains low.

"Builders are lowering prices to meet demand, and the median new home sales price remains well below the median existing home sales price," Berner said.

According to recent reports, the National Association of Home Builders found that new homes are nearly $40,000 less expensive than existing homes. Single-family housing starts rose 4% last month amid an uneven year. The latest Realtor.com quarterly construction insights report highlights that prices on new homes are holding steady, but builders are having to get creative to attract buyers.

Meanwhile, major homebuilders have reported large year-over-year declines in revenue. This week, the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index plunged to a 14-year low.

The tough environment has forced builders to get creative.

It has been revealed that "Builders are exercising caution, preferring to line up a buyer for their homes before starting work on them rather than building as many spec homes," Berner stated. "Newly introduced construction remains a strong alternative to the existing home segment, offering savings on mortgage rates, sale prices, and total cost of ownership.".

Sources indicate that simon Boag, CEO of Aro Homes, says his firm opted for across-the-board price cuts on its prefabricated homes, slashing about $12 million off the asking price of its overall housing stock. It ended up holding an auction to sell a batch of 10 homes, which seems to have worked. About eight of the homes found buyers.

Boag tells Realtor.com that he looks at past recessions when many buyers remained in the market, even if they weren't looking aggressively. Homebuilders have to accept lower margins, but there are buyers looking for homes.

"You look at a decent homebuilder margin in the 20% range, but at 17%, you're still a viable entity," Boag states. "The business model is about, 'OK markets move all the time,' and how do you deal with that.".

Recent findings suggest that for buyers, the market may have a higher barrier to entry in the high interest rate environment. That means preparation is essential.

Earlier this week, the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Index showed home values fell for the 16th straight month.

Jeffrey Ruben, president of home lending at WSFS Bank, expects the "tug of war" between high mortgage rates and affordability constraints limiting buyers in 2027.

Sources indicate that "While this is a good sign for home builders, it doesn't indicate what the market demonstrates as a whole," Ruben said. "We are seeing the data signal movement toward a buyer's market. This is seen more clearly through existing home sales with time on market, overall sales, and total inventory.".

He remarked buyers should be looking beyond standard resale listings and comparing the total monthly payment structure across both new and existing homes.

"Connecting with a lender early to evaluate builder incentives alongside traditional financing options can help buyers identify opportunities in the current market without stretching their household budget," he stated.

For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (831 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • How often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout.
  • The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues.
  • Depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout. A large study of Norwegian college students found that those who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety one year later. The findings suggest that maintaining a consistent exercise routine could be particularly vital for supporting mental well-being.

The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues. Their results point to the potential benefits of exercising regularly rather than focusing primarily on longer or more demanding workouts.

Why Exercise Habits Matter for Mental Health.

Depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide. The college years can be an especially challenging period as students adjust to upcoming academic, social, and personal responsibilities. Identifying everyday behaviors that may help protect mental health is therefore an important research priority.

Although previous research has linked regular physical activity to better psychological well-being, many young adults remain physically inactive. Scientists have also had relatively limited evidence about how exercise habits relate to the development of mental health conditions over time, particularly when those conditions are evaluated using standardized diagnostic tools.

In a recent development, to investigate this relationship, Grasdalsmoen and his team followed 10,460 full-time students enrolled in higher education in Norway. Participants ranged in age from 18 to 35.

Recent findings suggest that at the beginning of the study, students completed questionnaires describing their exercise habits, including how frequently they worked out, how strenuous their activities were, how long they exercised, and how many total hours they were active each week. One year later, they completed a self-administered diagnostic assessment designed to identify common mental health disorders.

Exercise Frequency May Matter More Than Intensity.

The researchers found that students who reported lower levels of physical activity were more likely to meet diagnostic criteria for anxiety or depression one year later. However, not every aspect of exercise showed the same relationship with mental health.

Exercise frequency emerged as a particularly consistent factor. How often students exercised was more reliably associated with their later mental health than the intensity of their workouts or the amount of time they spent exercising.

The researchers also identified differences between men and women. Among women, lower exercise intensity was associated with a greater likelihood of anxiety and depression. Among men, spending fewer total hours exercising each week revealed a stronger association with these conditions.

Overall, the likelihood of common mental health disorders decreased as weekly exercise increased, with this pattern continuing up to approximately 10 hours of physical activity per week.

The results also support the World Health Organization's recommendation that adults complete at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each week.

Regular Exercise Could Help Support Student Mental Health.

Recent findings suggest that taken together, the findings suggest that exercising consistently may be especially valuable for reducing the likelihood of anxiety and depression among college students. Rather than concentrating exclusively on workout intensity or duration, maintaining a regular routine could be an key part of supporting mental health.

However, the researchers emphasize that their observational study cannot establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship. Although students who exercised more regularly tended to have better mental health outcomes, the results do not prove that exercise itself prevented depression or anxiety.

It has been revealed that even with this limitation, promoting accessible opportunities for physical activity could be a useful part of broader efforts to improve student well-being. Such efforts may be especially relevant for students who are beginning to experience mental health difficulties or symptoms that have not yet reached the threshold for a clinical diagnosis.

Industry observers note that the authors add: "Our findings show that students who engage in regular physical exercise are at lower risk of developing common mental disorders over time. These findings highlight the importance of making physical activity an accessible and natural part of student life.".

"Mental health among students is a growing public health concern. Our findings suggest that supporting students to be physically active may contribute to better mental health and should be recognized as an notable part of a healthy learning environment.".

Recent findings suggest that funding: The SHoT study was financially supported by the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research (2017) and the Norwegian Ministry of Health and Care Services (2016). Neither funding organization participated in designing the research, collecting or analyzing data, deciding whether to publish the findings, or preparing the manuscript.

Anthropic is trying to kill traditional desktop apps with Claude-generated desktop apps

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (941 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, rarely a day goes by that Anthropic PBC doesn’t announce some kind of new capability, feature or model, and today wasn’t any different.
  • It promises to be one of its more impactful updates, fanning the flames of those who argue that artificial intelligence is ultimately destined to eat the software world.
  • The company said today that owners can now transform what it calls “artifacts” into standalone applications that run independently of Claude and can be accessed from the desktop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 21:36 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

According to recent reports, rarely a day goes by that Anthropic PBC doesn’t announce some kind of new capability, feature or model, and today wasn’t any different. Today came the ability to use Claude to create fully functional desktop applications for Windows and Mac computers with a single prompt.

It promises to be one of its more impactful updates, fanning the flames of those who argue that artificial intelligence is ultimately destined to eat the software world.

The company said today that owners can now transform what it calls “artifacts” into standalone applications that run independently of Claude and can be accessed from the desktop. Artifacts have been around for a while, and they can be almost anything, such as a simple order tracker or a meeting dashboard that pulls information from the user’s calendar and email inbox.

However, until today, artifacts were a bit tricky to access. They could be opened up only from inside Claude itself, which meant people first had to open up the chatbot, login and then find the old conversation where they originally created the artifact they want to use.

Anthropic noted people are using Claude artifacts all the time for various everyday tasks, and so it makes sense to mature the concept. “If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” the company said.

That’s why Anthropic is making it possible for people to use artifacts to create, run and share desktop applications with Claude’s newly introduced “Install as App” feature, which is available in beta now on Windows and macOS.

Industry observers note that in a video posted on X, Anthropic revealed how straightforward it is to create a functional desktop app from a simple prompt. The user simply describes the tool they want Claude to create, click confirm and then sit back and wait for a few seconds as it slaps together the required code to bring that app to life.

You can now install Claude artifacts as desktop apps on Mac and Windows.

Ask Claude to build an artifact, click "Install as app", and open it like any other app. It can use your connectors and, if you allow it, send notifications or add a menu bar item. pic.twitter.com/8CBgqe5OKq.

— ClaudeDevs (@ClaudeDevs) November 24, 2026.

Because these are “real” apps, they come with their own app icons and they open in a dedicated Window, rather than running within the Claude interface. They also get the ability to send notifications to customers, Anthropic stated.

Recent findings suggest that as an added benefit, Claude artifacts that are transformed into desktop apps will be able to use Claude and various third-party connectors, meaning that AI agents will be able to interact with them autonomously, Anthropic said. However, the firm did warn that any requests made by an app to Claude will count toward their monthly credit usage, which means it could become expensive if an app is used excessively.

In a blog post Anthropic showcased a number of examples of what its internal teams have built, including a fully featured image editing app called Linnet, a file manager with a cinematic design called Phosphor, and a terminal application that integrates with Claude, which is known as Tern.

There is one major caveat to Claude artifacts-as-apps that sets them apart from traditional desktop applications. According to Anthropic, “you need to be online and signed in to Claude to open an app.”.

That could be a pretty big downside, for many desktop applications are designed to work even if the computer is not connected to the internet. But those who lack a Wi-Fi connection will be unable to access their Claude-generated apps, even if they’re already built and configured.

Thanksgiving Nor’easter Postpones Macy’s Parade and Targets Over 250 Million: The Latest on Power Outages, Homes at Risk, and More

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A nor'easter and even a "bomb cyclone" are predicted to slam the Northeast on Thanksgiving this year, putting millions in a path of destruction not seen on the holiday for decades—and causing a time honored tradition to be postponed for the first time in its history.
  • Heavy rain, high winds, and coastal impacts to the East Coast are stated to begin on Wednesday and carry through Thanksgiving, according to NOAA's Weather Prediction Center.
  • The biggest impact will be seen starting in the Southeast, before moving its way to the Northeast, Great Lakes, and Ohio Valley.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A nor'easter and even a "bomb cyclone" are predicted to slam the Northeast on Thanksgiving this year, putting millions in a path of destruction not seen on the holiday for decades—and causing a time honored tradition to be postponed for the first time in its history.

Heavy rain, high winds, and coastal impacts to the East Coast are stated to begin on Wednesday and carry through Thanksgiving, according to NOAA's Weather Prediction Center.

The biggest impact will be seen starting in the Southeast, before moving its way to the Northeast, Great Lakes, and Ohio Valley.

While flooding is a major consideration, meteorologists are more concerned about the powerful winds accompanying the storm, which could result in tree damage, power outages, and other disasters for homeowners to contend with on the massive day.

According to recent reports, the high winds ultimately forced the hands of Latest York City officials, the NYPD and Macy's, who late on Wednesday unveiled that the parade would be pushed off until the following Saturday Nov. 28, due to the weather.

The storm will ramp up in the Southeast on Wednesday, according to The Weather Channel, with rain, wind, and coastal flooding causing hazardous conditions for travelers heading home for the holiday.

Because temperatures have dropped as well, snow is also likely in parts of Missouri and Illinois beginning later in the day, continuing into the night, into Thanksgiving.

By Thanksgiving Thursday, the storm will have made its way north into the mid-Atlantic and Ohio Valley, before steadily moving into Newly introduced England by afternoon or evening.

While wind is top of mind given the milestone parade, significant coastal flooding along the East Coast is poised to cause beach erosion, flooded coastal streets, and potential structural damage.

Moderate to major flooding is possible from Georgia to Long Island, alongside at least minor flooding in Newly introduced England, with any heavy rain during high tide worsening the inundation, notes Weather.com.

Peak water levels will hit Georgia and South Carolina on Wednesday morning, before shifting north to North Carolina, Virginia, Delaware, the Jersey Shore, and Long Island on Thanksgiving morning, and reaching coastal Latest England by Thursday and Friday midday.

Conditions could be especially severe in the mid-Atlantic, with widespread road flooding expected across Jersey Shore communities such as Atlantic City and Ocean City, water levels in Cape May and coastal Delaware potentially hitting their highest mark since January 2016, and Ocean City, MD, approaching its 1998 all-time record.

As the storm threatened to ground the balloons and drench the anticipated thousands of spectators, local outlets reported early Wednesday that Mayor Mamdani, the police commissioner and Macy's executives will announce the postponement of the Thanksgiving parade late on Wednesday.

The parade was scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST on Thursday, on Manhattan’s Upper West Side, and the National Weather Service had already issued a high wind warning before the call was made to move the parade.

The last reports predict that wind gusts will already exceed limits before the parade is even set to start.

"There is a significant risk that gusty winds ahead of the nor’easter cause the parade balloons to at least be lower than usual, and it’s possible they are not able to fly at all," AccuWeather Vice President of Forecast Operations Dan DePodwin noted ahead of the announcement .

Industry observers note that "This scenario is most likely should the storm move a bit more promptly up the coast. If it’s slower, the wind may intensify after the parade is over.".

Sustained winds must remain below 23 mph and gusts have to be lower than 34 mph for the balloons to fly.

The last balloon grounding was in 1971, but the parade has never been canceled due to weather in its 100-year history.

Power outages and tree damage are possible, according to the Weather Prediction Center, as wind gusts of 50-plus mph are forecasted along the coast with 40-plus mph gusts inland into the Interstate-95 corridor through at least Friday.

As of Monday evening, the National Weather Service warned that “tree damage and power outages will be possible” from the storm on Thanksgiving Day.

It has been revealed that the forecasts put the strongest gusts along the mid-Atlantic coast and inland corridors on Thursday. Along the Newly introduced Jersey shore and Delaware beaches, gusts will reach 50 to 60 mph—with 40 to 50 mph inland—prompting NWS Mount Holly to concern a high wind watch for the coastal strip from late Wednesday night through late Thursday night.

Farther south, Southeast Virginia and Northeast North Carolina face 2 to 3 inches of rain alongside east to northeast gusts of 40 to 50 mph inland and potentially 50 to 60 mph on the coast, where NWS Wakefield noted a high wind watch may be needed. Meanwhile, Washington, DC, Baltimore, and Northern Virginia can expect 1 to 3 inches of rain and Thanksgiving Day gusts of 35 to 50 mph, which NWS Sterling warned could be “strong to perhaps damaging.”.

The threat shifts northward later in the day, with Southern New England forecast to see gusts of 40 to 55 mph and up to 60 mph on Cape Cod and the islands. According to NWS Boston, the strongest winds in that region will arrive on Thursday night. In Rhode Island, forecasters specifically note the potential for isolated power outages late Thursday night and overnight, with coastal areas facing the highest risk.

Meanwhile, California has its own winter weather whirlwind to contend with, including massive waves battering the coastline.

According to the NWS, record-breaking king tides, combined with elevated surf and a large Pacific swell, are expected to bring significant coastal flooding to Southern California during this Thanksgiving week, with the greatest impacts anticipated Wednesday and Thursday, potentially flooding coastal properties and causing significant beach erosion.

“A series of winter storms is impacting California, bringing heavy rain, mountain snow, and potentially hazardous travel conditions,” the California Governor’s Office of Emergency Services said on Friday.

The mayor of San Francisco warned of “high tides and rain that this city has never seen before,” in the days leading up to the holiday, asking the public to avoid all but essential travel. The National Weather Service in the Bay Area added low areas would be prone to flooding, including San Francisco International Airport, which would be an added hindrance to travel to say the least.

Meanwhile, Southern California cities such as Newport Beach, Seal Beach, and Long Beach have put up miles of sand berms, some 15 feet tall or higher, to try to keep the ocean back, according to The Washington Post.

This weather seems to be a perfect storm of the warm waters of record-breaking El Niño colliding with an extra-high “king tide,” which the area already had to contend with a few weeks ago.

"In California, tides will be about half a foot higher than the highest in October," physical oceanographer Greg Dusek told Weather.com.

"This means that even if El Niño doesn't increase water levels further, there will be significant flooding along the California coast," Dusek noted.

Forecasts predict the worst of the storms could strike on Tuesday and Wednesday night into Thanksgiving Day.

Mastering the Art: How Real Estate Agents Should Write Facebook Ad Copy

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients.
  • It has been revealed that the first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience.
  • Sources indicate that the headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that consumers will see.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients. Among the various platforms available, Facebook remains a dominant force with its massive user base and advertising capabilities. To stand out in the competitive real estate market, agents must not only create compelling visual content but also craft persuasive ad copy that engages and captivates their target audience. In this article, we will delve into the key elements and strategies for writing effective Facebook ad copy, equipping real estate agents with the knowledge to maximize their advertising efforts and generate leads.

It has been revealed that the first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience. By knowing their demographics, preferences, and pain points, you can tailor your copy to resonate with their needs and desires. Conduct thorough market research, utilize Facebook's audience insights, and analyze data from previous campaigns to gather valuable information about your target audience.

Sources indicate that the headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that consumers will see. It needs to be attention-grabbing and compelling enough to entice people to read further. Use action-oriented words, emphasize unique selling propositions, and create a sense of urgency to pique the audience's curiosity and encourage them to click on your ad.

In a recent development, when writing Facebook ad copy, it's crucial to highlight the benefits of the property or service you're promoting, rather than merely listing its features. Benefits explain how the property or service can improve the lives of potential buyers or renters. By emphasizing the value and advantages, you can create an emotional connection with your audience and motivate them to take action.

Storytelling is a powerful tool for capturing the attention of your audience and making your Facebook ad copy more relatable. Craft a compelling narrative that showcases the unique aspects of the property or the positive experiences of previous clients. Engaging stories can evoke emotions, create a sense of authenticity, and build trust with potential clients.

Recent findings suggest that in the fast-paced world of social media, attention spans are limited. To ensure your Facebook ad copy is effective, keep it concise and clear. Use short sentences and paragraphs, bullet points, and subheadings to enhance readability. Avoid jargon and technical terms that may confuse or alienate your audience.

It has been revealed that social proof, such as testimonials, reviews, or success stories, can significantly influence potential clients' decision-making process. Incorporate social proof into your Facebook ad copy to build credibility and trust. Highlight positive feedback from satisfied clients or showcase awards and recognition you've received in the real estate industry.

According to recent reports, to encourage immediate action from your audience, create a sense of urgency in your Facebook ad copy. Limited-time offers exclusive deals, or a countdown timer can instill a fear of missing out (FOMO) and prompt potential clients to take the desired action promptly.

Industry observers note that an effective call-to-action (CTA) is vital to prompt people to take the desired action, whether it's contacting you, visiting a landing page, or scheduling a property viewing. Use action verbs, provide clear instructions, and create a sense of urgency to motivate users to click on your CTA button.

In a recent development, continuous testing and optimization are essential for improving the performance of your Facebook ad copy. Create multiple variations of your ad copy, test them against each other, and analyze the results. Fine-tune your copy based on metrics such as click-through rates (CTR), conversion rates, and engagement levels to identify what resonates best with your audience.

Writing compelling Facebook ad copy is a crucial skill for real estate agents looking to excel in their digital marketing efforts. By understanding their target audience, crafting attention-grabbing headlines, focusing on benefits, incorporating storytelling techniques, and utilizing social proof, agents can create persuasive and engaging copy that captivates potential clients. Remember to keep your copy concise and clear, create a sense of urgency, and use compelling calls to action. Through A/B testing and continuous optimization, agents can refine their ad copy to maximize its effectiveness. By mastering the art of writing Facebook ad copy, real estate agents can unlock the full potential of social media advertising and boost their success in the competitive real estate market.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All season long, the "Dancing with the Stars" judges recognized Amber Glenn's competitive nature, but now that the season has come to an end, the Olympic figure skater is proving that she has been a team player all along.

Glen came in second place in the competition dance series, with two-time Paralympian Ezra Frech taking home the coveted Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy.

And while the contestants share a spot on Team USA—for which they've both brought home gold medals—they quickly bonded in the competition as their professional dance partners, Pasha Pashkov and Daniella Karagach, are married.

When asked how she felt about the results after the finale, Glenn told Extra she "couldn't ask for a better result," and described a "triumphant feeling" as she walked away from Season 35 having earned 10s across the board in all three of her final performances.

Recent findings suggest that "From day one, we all met up, had a little dinner over at their house, and we noted, 'We wanna go 1-2,'" she explained to the outlet. "And we didn't specify, like, whatever happens, happens, but the fact that we came in here and we both got those perfect scores. We both did everything we could and it was truly in the hands of the people at home. I'm really proud of what we did and I'm really, really happy that Team USA took it home.".

The group—who have been unofficially dubbed "Team USA and the Pashkovs" by fans and even the official U.S. Olympic and Paralmypic team all season—have been close collaborators throughout the competition.

According to recent reports, during the Nov. 10 episode, when teams were paired off and required to compete in two-on-two dance-offs, Glenn and Pashkov and Frech and Karagach put a friendly spin on the format by switching partners mid-choreography as they performed a Rumba to "The Boy Is Mine" by Brandy and Monica.

"It felt more like a team dance than anything else," Karagach told Us magazine. "We came together ,and we had the best time sharing the dance floor, and we couldn't also not end swapping partners because I've always wanted to dance with Amber, and Ezra and Pasha secretly wanted to dance with each other. So that was fun.".

The competitors-turned-pals took to social media to share plenty of heartwarming behind-the-scenes moments throughout the experience, providing a glimpse at what their down time is like between rehearsals. In one Sept. 18 post, Pashkov wrote, "We're a tightly-knit fam now.".

Recent findings suggest that in a post-finale interview with Deadline, Glenn described the moment she had realized Frech would win. The Plano, TX native stated, "I don't know if I felt as many emotions watching a performance as I did when watching Ezra and Dani. It was like, at first, it's excitement. I'm like, 'I love that Linkin Park [song].' And then horror, fear, and like, panic.'".

Sources indicate that the moment Glenn was referring to was the malfunction in which Frech's prosthetic fell off mid-performance. Frech and Karagach promptly communicated while dancing, allowing him to secure it into place properly and complete the routine.

"I think I gasped so loud I threw my rib out again," Glenn continued. "So then, the physical pain and just like, fear, panic, and then just awe, inspiration, something you feel in your core. I know that's a saying, but like you feel it in your gut, and it takes your breath away, and that's what it was.".

Glenn said that in that moment, she "was like, 'They won.'" She even added that she "would feel bad" if she had taken home the trophy after seeing Frech and Karagach pull off "such a perfect dance" after "working so hard for it all season.".
